beats.text: A dead "Royal Marines officer" carried fake invasion plans.
beats.note: The body was released from the submarine HMS Seraph so that it would be found. A fisherman found it.
British Military Intelligence invented him. His papers pointed to landings in Greece and Sardinia, with Sicily as a feint.

beats.text: A letter between two generals named the wrong targets.
beats.note: It called Sicily and the Dodecanese "cover targets" for the real assaults.

beats.text: Germany moved forces to the wrong places.
beats.note: Reinforcements went to Greece and Sardinia before and during the invasion of Sicily. Sicily received none.

beats.text: The body was never an officer.
beats.note: In 1996 it was identified as Glyndwr Michael, a Welsh homeless man.

beats.name: Roger Morgan
beats.role: An amateur historian from London who found the evidence in the Public Record Office.

beats.text: He was buried with full military honours as Major Martin.
beats.note: In 1998 a new inscription was added to the stone after the identification.

beats.text: He fooled an army in death, and his real name stayed hidden for over fifty years.

beats.line: A lie needs a believable paper trail.
